query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these incident tickets.

per_column.name: affected_system
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the system domain from short_description, giving a strong grouping axis for triage/volume analysis. Samples (database, vpn, internet_connectivity, os_software) are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: symptom_type
per_column.rationale: A distinct failure-mode axis orthogonal to affected_system, useful for pattern analysis. Sample mappings (no_access, unstable_intermittent, not_working_generic) are well-grounded in the descriptions.

per_column.name: incident_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual vs infrastructure-wide) is analytically valuable for impact prioritization, but the short descriptions rarely state scope explicitly. Labels like 'infrastructure_wide' for 'Internet connection unstable' and 'individual_user' for 'Unable to access the database' appear to be unsupported inferences from silent text.

per_column.name: is_open_unresolved
per_column.rationale: Derivable from existing state/closed_at columns, so largely redundant with original data; adds little new analytical leverage. Values are well-grounded (closed_at populated => not open).

per_column.name: self_resolved
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident self-resolved is analytically interesting, but nothing in the sampled source text supports a self_resolved determination; 'Unable to access company intranet' marked True has no textual basis, suggesting weakly grounded inference.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Near-constant (472 True / 28 False), so it provides almost no discriminating power. It is also marked True for one-off phrasings like 'Unable to access the database' with no recurrence wording, indicating an unsupported label.

per_column.name: opened_hour_of_day
per_column.rationale: Temporal bucketing gives a genuine axis for load/timing analysis. Grounded in opened_at, though the samples only expose sys_updated_on/closed_at; buckets are plausible and warranted from a timestamp.

per_column.name: access_context
per_column.rationale: Remote vs on-premise is a useful axis, especially for VPN/connectivity tickets. Mostly labeled 'unspecified' (a correct silent-row value) with 'remote' warranted for VPN, so groundedness is reasonable.

judge.rationale: The strongest columns (affected_system, symptom_type, opened_hour_of_day, access_context) provide genuine, orthogonal grouping axes well-grounded in the ticket text and timestamps. Weaknesses: is_open_unresolved is largely redundant with existing state/closed_at; recurrence_signal is near-constant and its True labels are not supported by the short descriptions; incident_scope and self_resolved make confident assertions the terse source text does not warrant. Overall a useful but partly over-asserting augmentation.
